TASK GOAL

Audit the Freshdesk support queue for exposed sensitive data while distinguishing authorized disclosures. Draft compliance findings for user review before any redaction or external notice.

NECESSARY INPUTS / EVIDENCE

- Freshdesk queue contents and available ticket metadata, attachments, conversations, requester details, and disclosure context.
- Applicable support-domain criteria for sensitive data exposure and evidence showing whether each disclosure was authorized.
- Existing workspace artifacts or policies relevant to compliance classification.
- Excluded stale artifacts must be omitted.

VISIBLE WORK TO COMPLETE

- Independently inspect the Freshdesk queue using available workspace tools.
- Identify tickets or artifacts containing potentially exposed sensitive data.
- Determine whether each disclosure is authorized based on available evidence; clearly distinguish confirmed findings from unresolved cases.
- Draft concise compliance findings with ticket or case identifiers, affected data categories, exposure context, authorization status, risk, and recommended next steps.
- Do not redact data, alter tickets, contact external parties, or issue notices.

COMPLETED STEP SUMMARY

- No audit, evidence collection, classification, redaction, or notification work has been completed.

CURRENT BRANCH TOOL RESULTS

- No tool results are available. Retrieve or recompute all necessary evidence independently using visible workspace tools.

COMPLETION CONTRACT

- Use the available Freshdesk and workspace inspection/search tools to review the support queue and gather only the evidence necessary for classification.
- Produce a review-ready compliance findings artifact covering confirmed exposures, authorized disclosures, unresolved authorization questions, and recommended remediation.
- Stop after drafting the findings for user review; perform no redaction, ticket modification, external notice, or other remediation action.
- Return a short final answer identifying the completed review artifact and summarizing the principal findings without unnecessarily reproducing sensitive data.

UNCERTAINTY POLICY

- Do not infer authorization or exposure without supporting evidence.
- Mark missing or ambiguous authorization evidence as unresolved and state what evidence is needed.
- Minimize sensitive data in notes and findings; use ticket or case references and data-category descriptions rather than reproducing exposed values.
- Omit excluded stale artifacts.
